## Final natural-language hypothesis
**"Individuals with a criminal record (proxy: jailed 1985–1994, ever_jailed==1) had significantly lower wealth than those without a criminal record in 1985, 1990, and 1996 (two-sided Mann–Whitney U with Holm–Bonferroni adjustment across the three years at α=0.05; median wealth in the criminal-record group was lower in 3/3 years)."**

## What was executed (analysis.py, run successfully)
**Data:** data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv, 12,013 rows, no missing values. Criminal-record proxy = ever_jailed==1 (n=289) vs no-record (n=11,724). Residence-based "Jail" gauge explicitly noted as **not applicable** — the file has only the 6 documented columns (no residence field).

**Per-year primary (Mann–Whitney U, two-sided, jailed vs no-record):**
| Year | p_raw | p_Holm | Cliff's d | median diff (jailed − other) | 95% boot CI of median diff | Significant (holm<0.05, lower) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 1.60e-10 | 1.60e-10 | −0.218 | −2,880 | [−3,600, −2,300] | YES |
| 1990 | 7.80e-35 | 2.34e-34 | −0.420 | −10,500 | [−11,153, −10,000] | YES |
| 1996 | 9.28e-26 | 1.86e-25 | −0.351 | −8,500 | [−9,950, −7,200] | YES |

**Sensitivity — conclusions hold across all tests (3/3 per year):**
- Part A (χ² on wealth ≤0 vs >0): 1985 p=3.4e-6; 1990 p=3.6e-23; 1996 p=1.8e-17. P(wealth≤0) record vs no-record: 45.0 vs 31.8% (1985), 56.7 vs 29.2% (1990), 63.0 vs 40.4% (1996) — jailed group far more likely to hold zero/negative wealth.
- Part B (Mann–Whitney on strictly positive wealth only): all p<0.05, Cliff's d still negative (−0.25, −0.46, −0.49) — the gap is not merely driven by zeros.
- Part C (Welch t on log1p(wealth+offset)): all p<0.05 (t = −9.4, −11.1, −15.9).

**Descriptives (jailed vs no-record):** 1985 mean 7,929 vs 25,086, median 720 vs 3,600; 1990 mean 16,350 vs 73,948, median 0 vs 10,500; 1996 mean 20,383 vs 105,447, median 0 vs 8,500.

**Caveat noted in deliverable:** all three years show statistically significant lower wealth for the criminal-record proxy group, with the largest effect in 1990 and 1996 (Cliff's d ≈ −0.42/−0.35) and a visible increase in the jailed group's zero/negative-wealth share over time. The analysis is unadjusted; race/sex confounding (jailed group skews black/male) remains a stated limitation.
